text:
Alicia M: FYI ran a 10k-req soak on mixtral-moe after the kernel upgrade, saw router CPU jumps and KV cache miss storms around p95. attaching profile snippet.
Ben K: can you paste the flamegraph or top hotspots?
Alicia M: gist: top is `router::dispatch_batch` and `kv_cache::evict_if_needed`. spikes coincide with batches hitting top-k > 32.
Diego R: important: kernel 2.1 changed matmul tiling and slightly increased latency variance for small heads. could amplify router jitter.
Priya S: interesting — did batching heuristics change? iirc we moved to dynamic micro-batches (adaptive batcher).
Alicia M: yes, adaptive batcher is doing more aggressive coalescing. average batch size up ~18 -> good throughput but tail suffers when experts are imbalanced.
Ben K: hypothesis: larger batches increase per-request KV pressure because more unique prefixes keep KV cache warm, leading to thrash + eviction churn. that explains `kv_cache::evict_if_needed`.
Priya S: any change in top-k routing config? we're on topk=64 for some customers.
Alicia M: some heavy clients still routing topk=64; combined with `router_softmax_temp=1.2` we see more spread across experts -> more distinct KVs.
Diego R: profiling notes: when topk>32, calls to `expert_forward` increase 2.5x and GPU kernel launch overhead + memcpy shows up.
infra-bot: deploybot: rollout v2.1.3 -> mixtral-runtime completed to canary(10%).
Ben K: perf regression appears in canary traces too. can we pin canary to older kernel and rerun?
Alicia M: already tested quick rollback to kernel 2.0.8: tail latency normalized and KV miss rate dropped ~42%.
Priya S: good repro. next: figure tradeoffs so we don't lose throughput. options: 1) tune top-k per-customer; 2) adjust router_softmax_temp; 3) change batching heuristic to cap micro-batch size when expert imbalance detected; 4) KV cache eviction tuning (LRU windows).
Diego R: also consider `expert_parallelism` knob: currently set to 2 for 48-expert models. bumping to 4 spreads work but increases cross-device comms and KV dependency. for some request profiles it's net negative. need microbenchmarks.
Alicia M: did a quick sim: limiting topk to 32 for worst offenders reduced expert invocations by ~35% and reduced dispatch latency p95 by ~220ms.
Ben K: propose an adaptive router policy: use a cheap locality estimator on prefix hashes to prefer same-expert affinity for repeated prefixes, falling back to global top-k when confidence low. should reduce KV churn.
Priya S: love that. we can implement heuristic in router (cpu) without touching kernel. small perf win, low risk.
Diego R: action items: (A) Priya prototype affinity heuristic, (B) Ben run microbench with expert_parallelism={1,2,4} across batch sizes [8,16,32], (C) Alicia coordinate canary rollback until fix.
Alicia M: timeline: Priya - prototype by EOD tomorrow; Ben - microbench results in 48h; I'll pin canary now.
infra-bot: incidentbot: rollback initiated by Alicia M for canary pool.
Ben K: also stash the flamegraphs and raw perf counters in s3://redwood-perf/mixtral/kernel-2.1/2123456789/
Priya S: small config note: reduce `router_softmax_temp` to 0.9 for the clients we limit topk on; should concentrate probability mass. test in perf sim.
Alicia M: adding example command for reproducer:
```
# reproduce with 10k mixed-length requests
./perf_driver --model mixtral-7b-moe --topk 64 --softmax_temp 1.2 --batcher adaptive --parallelism 2 --requests 10000 --profile out.json
```
Ben K: thanks — i'll run that locally and share flamegraphs.
Diego R: one more thought: RoPE scaling (we had a change in seqlen handling recently) — for long sequences it increases attention compute and may exacerbate lat tails on batches that mix short/long seqs. check correlation seqlen vs tail.
Alicia M: good call. adding seqlen histogram to reproducer.
Priya S: optional short-term mitigation: per-client routing caps + best-effort KV prefetch when affinity detected.
Alicia M: agreed. owners + followups in thread. ping me if you need GPU slots. :thumbsup:
